items.title: Section: The Chapter on Arising the Resolve Opens — Five Aspects of Bodhicitta

items.zh: 菩薩最初發心，於諸菩薩所有正願是初正願，普能攝受其餘正願，是故發心以初正願為其自性。
items.en: A bodhisattva's initial resolve is, among all a bodhisattva's genuine aspirations, the very first — and it comprehensively gathers in every aspiration that follows. For this reason, the arising of the resolve has this first aspiration as its own nature.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩起正願心求菩提時，發如是心，說如是言：願我決定當證無上正等菩提，能作有情一切義利。畢竟安處究竟涅槃及以如來廣大智中。如是發心，定自希求無上菩提，及求能作有情義利，是故發心以定希求為其行相。
items.en: When bodhisattvas raise this genuine aspiration and seek awakening, they give rise to this very thought and speak these very words: may I definitely attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, be able to accomplish every benefit for beings, and ultimately settle them in final nirvāṇa and in the Tathāgata's vast wisdom. Since such an arising of the resolve is a definite wish for unsurpassed awakening and for the capacity to benefit beings, the arising of the resolve has this definite wish as its mode.

items.title: The Resolve's Remaining Three Aspects — Its Object, Its Virtue, and Why Nothing Surpasses It

items.zh: 又諸菩薩緣大菩提，及緣有情一切義利，發心希求，非無所緣，是故發心以大菩提及諸有情一切義利為所緣境。
items.en: Bodhisattvas take great awakening, and every benefit for beings, as the object of this resolve and wish — it is never a wish with no object at all. For this reason, the arising of the resolve has great awakening and every being's benefit as its object.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩最初發心，能攝一切菩提分法殊勝善根為上首故，是善、極善，是賢、極賢，是妙、極妙，能違一切有情處所三業惡行功德相應。又諸菩薩最初發心所起正願，於餘一切希求世間、出世間義妙善正願，最為第一，最為無上。
items.en: The initial resolve is able to gather in every excellent wholesome root belonging to the factors of awakening as its very forefront — it is wholesome, and supremely wholesome; virtuous, and supremely virtuous; sublime, and supremely sublime … among every other aspiration seeking excellent, wholesome ends, mundane or supramundane, the genuine aspiration that arises with a bodhisattva's initial resolve is foremost, is unsurpassed.

items.zh: 如是應知最初發心有五種相。一者、自性，二者、行相，三者、所緣，四者、功德，五者、最勝。

items.title: What the Resolve Actually Does — Entry, Root, Compassion's Overflow, and the Ground of All Training

items.zh: 又諸菩薩初發心已，即名趣入無上菩提，預在大乘諸菩薩數。此據世俗言說道理，是故發心趣入所攝。又諸菩薩要發心已，方能漸次速證無上正等菩提，非未發心，是故發心能為無上菩提根本。
items.en: Once bodhisattvas first raise the resolve, they are immediately said to have entered upon unsurpassed awakening, already reckoned among the great vehicle's bodhisattvas — this is stated according to conventional usage. For this reason, the resolve is included as entry itself … only once the resolve has been raised are bodhisattvas gradually able to swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening — never without it. For this reason, the resolve serves as the very root of unsurpassed awakening.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩悲愍一切有苦眾生，為欲濟拔，發菩提心，是故發心是悲等流。又諸菩薩以初發心為所依止、為建立故，普於一切菩提分法及作一切有情義利菩薩學中皆能修學，是故發心是諸菩薩學所依止。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, out of compassion for every suffering being, wishing to rescue them, raise the resolve for awakening — for this reason, the resolve is compassion's own overflow … bodhisattvas, taking the initial resolve as basis and foundation, are thereby able to train fully in every factor of awakening and in every training that benefits beings — for this reason, the resolve is the very basis of a bodhisattva's training.

items.zh: 如是應知最初發心是趣入攝、菩提根本、大悲等流、學所依止。

items.title: Two Kinds of Resolve, and Why Some Falls Are Final While Others Are Not

items.zh: 又諸菩薩最初發心略有二種。一者、永出，二、不永出。言永出者，謂發心已畢竟隨轉，無復退還。不永出者，謂發心已不極隨轉，而復退還。
items.en: A bodhisattva's initial resolve is, in brief, of two kinds: permanently departing, and not permanently departing … permanently departing means that, once the resolve is raised, it continues without exception, never again reverting. Not permanently departing means that, once raised, it does not continue in full, and reverts once again.

items.zh: 此發心退復有二種。一者、究竟，二、不究竟。究竟退者，謂一退已，不能復發求菩提心。不究竟者，謂退已後，數數更發求菩提心。
items.en: This falling-back of the resolve is again of two kinds: final, and not final … final falling-back means that, once fallen, one is no longer able to raise the aspiration for awakening again … not final means that, having fallen, one again and again raises the aspiration for awakening once more.

items.zh: 當知菩薩最初發心，由四種緣、四因、四力。云何四緣？

items.title: Section: Four Conditions That Spark the Resolve — Wonder, Teaching, Loss, and a Degenerate Age's Suffering

items.zh: 謂善男子或善女人，若見諸佛及諸菩薩，有不思議甚奇希有神變威力，或從可信聞如是事。既見聞已，便作是念：無上菩提具大威德，令安住者及修行者，成就如是所見所聞不可思議神變威力。由此見聞增上力故，於大菩提深生信解，因斯發起大菩提心。是名第一初發心緣。
items.en: Should a son or daughter of good family see the buddhas and bodhisattvas display inconceivable, wondrous, rare, and powerful miraculous transformations … by the strengthened power of this seeing or hearing, deep confidence arises in great awakening, and from this the great resolve for awakening is raised. This is the first condition for the initial resolve.

items.zh: 或有一類，雖不見聞如前所說神變威力，而聞宣說依於無上正等菩提微妙正法菩薩藏教，聞已深信；由聞正法及與深信增上力故，於如來智深生信解，為得如來微妙智故，發菩提心。是名第二初發心緣。
items.en: There is another who, without seeing or hearing such wondrous power, hears instead the sublime true teaching of the bodhisattva canon, resting on unsurpassed, perfect awakening itself … by the strengthened power of hearing the true teaching and the deep confidence it brings, profound confidence arises in the Tathāgata's wisdom, and, wishing to attain that same sublime wisdom, the resolve for awakening is raised. This is the second condition.

items.zh: 或有一類，雖不聽聞如上正法，而見一切菩薩藏法將欲滅沒。見是事已，便作是念：菩薩藏法久住於世，能滅無量眾生大苦，我應住持菩薩藏法，發菩提心，為滅無量眾生大苦。
items.en: There is another who, without having heard such teaching directly, sees the entire bodhisattva canon on the verge of vanishing from the world … [and reflects:] if the bodhisattva canon remains long in the world, it is able to end boundless beings' great suffering; I should uphold and preserve the bodhisattva canon, raising the resolve for awakening, in order to end boundless beings' great suffering.

items.zh: 由為護持菩薩藏法增上力故，於如來智深生信解，為得如來微妙智故，發菩提心。是名第三初發心緣。
或有一類，雖不觀見正法欲滅，而於末劫、末世、末時，見諸濁惡眾生身心，十隨煩惱之所惱亂。
items.en: There is another who, without observing the true teaching itself on the verge of vanishing, sees, in a degenerate eon, a degenerate age, a degenerate time, beings whose bodies and minds are corrupted and afflicted, disturbed by derivative affliction in ten ways.

blocks.text: The arising of the resolve for awakening (bodhicitta, 發菩提心): its nature, object, and causes. This chapter has been read and commented on for over a thousand years.

"A bodhisattva's initial resolve is, among all genuine aspirations, the very first, and gathers in every aspiration that follows." Its words: "May I definitely attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, be able to accomplish every benefit for beings, and ultimately establish them in nirvāṇa and the Tathāgata's wisdom."
"Great awakening and every being's benefit" are its object; "it is never a wish with no object". It is "wholesome and supremely wholesome; virtuous and supremely virtuous".

"Once bodhisattvas first raise the resolve, they are said to have entered upon unsurpassed awakening", counted among the great vehicle. It is the root of all bodhisattva training. "Out of compassion for every suffering being, wishing to rescue them, they raise the resolve: hence it is compassion's own overflow."
The resolve may be **permanently departing** (never reverting) or not. A fall may be **final** (never raised again) or not (raised again and again).

One raises the resolve: on seeing or hearing of the Buddhas' and bodhisattvas' wonders; on hearing the bodhisattva teachings; on seeing those teachings about to vanish ("I should uphold and preserve them"); or on seeing "in a degenerate age, beings whose bodies and minds are corrupted".

quiz.q: "The very first aspiration, gathering all the others." The note calls it the second of five. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: the five are resolve, rebirth, conduct, genuine, and great vows; the first, resolve, gathers the other four
quiz.why: "A bodhisattva's initial resolve is, among all a bodhisattva's genuine aspirations, the very first — and it comprehensively gathers in every aspiration that follows." Master Cháng Bǎi: the five are the vow of resolve, of rebirth, of conduct, the genuine vow, and the great vow; the initial vow of resolve gathers the other four. The note's "second" is wrong.

quiz.q: The vow to "accomplish every benefit for beings" — whom does "beings" mainly mean here, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: only gods and humans, the most able to learn the noble path
quiz.why: "May I definitely attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, be able to accomplish every benefit for beings." Master Cháng Bǎi: "beings" here means only gods and humans, mainly because they are most able to learn the noble path.

quiz.q: The initial resolve is "wholesome, supremely wholesome; virtuous, supremely virtuous; sublime, supremely sublime." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "supremely"?
options: good upon good, virtuous upon virtuous, sublime upon sublime
quiz.why: "It is wholesome, and supremely wholesome; virtuous, and supremely virtuous; sublime, and supremely sublime." Master Cháng Bǎi: good upon good, hence supremely good; virtuous upon virtuous, hence supremely virtuous; sublime upon sublime, hence supremely sublime.

quiz.q: "Once the resolve is raised, one is said to have entered upon awakening … according to conventional usage." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this means?
options: not the great bodhisattva's attainment of non-arising acceptance or irreversibility
quiz.why: "Once bodhisattvas first raise the resolve, they are immediately said to have entered upon unsurpassed awakening … this is stated according to conventional usage." Venerable Miào Jìng: it doesn't mean he has attained acceptance of non-arising and irreversibility — not that great bodhisattva's state.

quiz.q: "Out of compassion for suffering beings … the resolve is compassion's overflow." What two motives does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish?
options: one for unsurpassed awakening, one to rescue beings
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, out of compassion for every suffering being, wishing to rescue them, raise the resolve for awakening — for this reason, the resolve is compassion's own overflow." Venerable Miào Jìng: one raises the resolve seeking unsurpassed awakening; the other raises it to rescue beings.

quiz.q: "Not final: having fallen, one again and again raises the aspiration." Why can one raise it again, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "Not final means that, having fallen, one again and again raises the aspiration for awakening once more." Venerable Miào Jìng: one can still raise the resolve — because of the lineage.

quiz.q: The third condition: seeing the bodhisattva canon about to vanish. What marks this person, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: especially strong compassion — seeing wrong views spread, raising the resolve to protect the canon
quiz.why: "I should uphold and preserve the bodhisattva canon, raising the resolve for awakening, in order to end boundless beings' great suffering." Master Cháng Bǎi: such people have especially strong compassion; seeing outsiders' wrong views prevail, they raise the resolve to protect the bodhisattva canon.
